advisory.finding: test_det_check_has_no_world_measurement_reach asserts a security/isolation property by grepping the SOURCE UNDER TEST for forbidden substrings ('boto3','subprocess','requests',...) rather than by exercising behavior. This is source-grepping: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (a legitimate non-network subprocess use, or the token appearing in a comment) and is blind to an actual network call reached via an indirect/transitive import or getattr — the very regression it purports to guard.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Narrow test_rubric_states_all_four_decision_rules to the machine-consumed field identifiers only (or drop the prose-wording 'no-anchor'/'no comparable' substring guard), since an LLM consuming the rubric is not a non-human parser and the wording is not a contract token.
evidence: assert "no-anchor" in body or "no comparable" in body, "rule (b) no-anchor fallback missing"
Rubric prose the token guards: '.rebar/prompts/plan-review-project-measurement-provenance.md:40  RULE (b) — THE NO-ANCHOR FALLBACK. If the repository offers NO comparable anchor'
Rule-5 litmus: the grepped token is a real contract only if a NON-HUMAN consumer branches on the exact value; the rubric body is consumed by an LLM, which is not a non-human consumer.
advisory.finding: test_rubric_states_all_four_decision_rules greps the rubric prompt (.md) for prose-wording tokens whose only consumer is an LLM. The rule-(b) clause `"no-anchor" in body or "no comparable" in body` guards the author's wording, not a contract token read by a non-human parser, so it is a change-detector: a behavior-preserving rewording of the rubric that preserves the LLM's instruction would break the test.
